## 1. No recruiting contact identified — still unanswered

**Boston College — the only school with NO usable direct contact.** Named a likely recruiter (Mathew Johnson, Asst.) but every email/phone cell on the MBB coaches page and the athletics directory is blank — apparently deliberate, since BC prints @bc.edu addresses for admins and even for the *women's* DBO. Only route is the recruit questionnaire. Switchboard 617-552-3000. (Remick/Jones addresses in the scout notes are media + compliance, not recruiting — do not use.)

**Four schools have emails but NO identified recruiting lead** — nobody flagged as the portal/personnel person, so first contact is a guess among assistants:
- **Northeastern** — 4 published emails; Coen has none. No GM/DoPP.
- **UMass** — 9 published emails; no questionnaire exists (all URLs 404). Best guesses only: Allen Edwards (assoc. HC), Brian Steele, Jake Hayden.
- **Cornell** — program inbox menshoops@cornell.edu + 4 staff; head coach has no personal address; no live questionnaire.
- **Le Moyne** — 4 emails incl. head coach; questionnaire exists but **reported closed / not accepting submissions on 2026-08-29**.

**Also unresolved:** Syracuse publishes McNamara's email as **jmmcbrid@syr.edu — the identical address listed for Jill McBride, Office Coordinator.** That is a gatekeeper inbox, not the head coach. Use GM Greg Fahey (grfahey@syr.edu) — Syracuse's own 2026-05-01 release names portal management as his job.

**Head coaches with no published email anywhere** (contact the assistants, don't construct an address): Holy Cross (Paulsen), Northeastern (Coen), Yale (Jones), Fairfield (Casey), Cornell (Jaques), BC (all staff), Syracuse (effectively). Address patterns at BU, Northeastern and Fairfield are internally inconsistent and cannot be extrapolated.

## 2. Staleness to re-check

**No school needs a full staff re-pull** — all 13 as_of dates are 2026-08-28/29 pulls off the schools' own 2026-27 pages. The stale items are narrower:

- **Northeastern** — staff *table* is current, staff *bios* are 2024-dated (Smith's still says "2024-25"). Contract info is from **2010**. Re-check Coen's status before writing.
- **Sacred Heart** — Steinway bio not refreshed since 2024-25; two current players' bios blank; transfer cycles were reconstructed by roster diff, not school releases.
- **Harvard** — the recruiting-form page has a **2020 URL path** and still calls Sotsky "Assistant Coach" (he's Associate HC). Email confirmed on the 2026 page; the form page itself is old — verify it's still monitored before mailing a PDF.
- **Boston College / Le Moyne** — 2024 and 2025 transfer histories came from **Wikipedia**, not primary sources. Softer than the rest.
- **Syracuse** — camp info stale (last confirmed release 2025-05-13, branded to the fired coach); 2024 transfer class is beat-sourced only.
- **UMass** — contract terms are June-2024 reporting.
- **Holy Cross** — Paulsen's bio prose still reads "third season" (Sidearm lag only; the staff table is verified 2026-27).
- **Colgate** — the URL in the original task (gocolgateraiders.com) is wrong; correct domain is **colgateathletics.com**. Fix wherever that's stored.

## 3. Coaching-change / hot-seat flags

**No coach in the set is reported departed or on a hot seat.** Two contacts were already reset this spring:

- **Boston College** — Earl Grant fired 2026-03-08; **Luke Murray** hired 2026-03-26. Entire staff assembled Apr–Aug 2026. Year two by a 2027-28 arrival.
- **Syracuse** — Adrian Autry fired 2026-03-11; **Gerry McNamara** hired 2026-03-24. Year two by 2027-28.

**Two to monitor, unreported but materially exposed:**
- **Northeastern (Coen)** — 7-24 (2-16 CAA) last year, ~306-323 career, 21st season, no public contract since 2010. A change before 2027-28 is plausible; nothing is reported either way.
- **Holy Cross (Paulsen)** — 11-22 (5-13), picked 9th in the preseason poll, contract length unpublished.

Most secure: Yale (Jones, 28th yr, back-to-back Ivy titles), Harvard (Amaker, 20th yr, incoming NABC president), Colgate (Langel, extended through 2030, USA Basketball U18 staff), UMass (Martin, extension through 2028-29).

## 4. Non-D1 pattern

**Proven D3 precedent — the only three:**
- **BU** — *Alex Zakheim, 6'1" G, Brandeis (D3, UAA) → BU, this exact cycle,* on the 2026-27 roster. Plus two D2 guards (SNHU, Maryville). Directly comparable, and BU also has the best published-email access in the set.
- **Sacred Heart** — strongest overall volume: **five below-D1 guards in four cycles** (D2 SNHU, Wilmington, West Chester; JUCO Orange County CC, NW Kansas Tech), two on the current roster — plus a D3 precedent in Alex Sobel (Middlebury, D3 National POY).
- **Yale** — Connor May, WashU (D3) → Yale 2026-27, and he is the *only* college transfer Yale took in five years. Forward, not guard, n=1. Move was "pending admissions" — Ivy has no grad eligibility, so it must clear undergrad transfer admissions.

**Below-D1 door open, D3 unproven** (all D2/JUCO only):
- **Holy Cross** — three straight cycles; Paulsen said so on the record. D2/JUCO guards only, no D3.
- **UMass** — three D2/JUCO guards in the 2025 class alone. No D3 or NAIA on any roster 2023-27.
- **Cornell** — all three of its last guard transfers came from below D1 (D2 Lock Haven, 2 JUCO). No D3. Ivy admissions gate applies.
- **Fairfield** — JUCO guards in three straight cycles; zero D2/D3/NAIA ever found.
- **Le Moyne** — JUCO guards ×2 cycles, one NAIA forward. No D2/D3. (Was itself D2 until 2023-24 — old D2 names on rosters are holdovers, not a pipeline.)

**Clearly do not take non-D1 players:**
- **Boston College** — every transfer 2024/2025/2026 came from D1. Confirmed no, not unknown.
- **Northeastern** — 10 for 10 D1 across three cycles. Their non-D1 pipeline is prep/international, a different door.
- **Syracuse** — all D1 direct. The one below-D1 career (Nate Kingz: NAIA → JUCO → Oregon State) reached them only *after* a D1 waypoint.
- **Colgate** — no below-D1 addition in four cycles, ~1 transfer per cycle total, one cycle with zero; a prep-freshman program. The lone 2026 transfer is the George Mason head coach's son.
- **Harvard** — structurally closed, not just unlikely: ~a dozen College transfer admits per year, "none of them typically athletes"; Ivy bars grad competition; **zero** incoming transfers of any kind in three cycles. Harvard is an outflow program.

**Priority ordering that falls out:** BU and Sacred Heart are the only two with both a D3 precedent *and* a clean published email route. Yale is third but gated by admissions. BC's contact gap is the single biggest open item; Le Moyne's closed questionnaire and UMass's missing questionnaire are the next two.

RECRUITING LEAD — read this caveat. Yale publishes NO formal recruiting title: no recruiting coordinator, no general manager, no director of player personnel. Derrick Seldon is "Director of Operations," not basketball ops recruiting. I set handles_recruiting=true on Matt Kingsley as an inference from evidence, not from a published designation. Supporting evidence: his official Yale bio says "Kingsley has traveled the country recruiting high-quality student-athletes to Yale," credits him with having "recruited and mentored five Ivy League Players of the Year," and cites a Top 25 Mid-Major Assistant Coach Recruiter selection (CoachStat.Net); a Jan 2026 Hoops HQ profile credits Jones's staff — Kingsley, Carberry, Sherrod — with recruiting the players who fit Ivy academic/athletic demands. He is also the senior assistant and one of only two staff with both a published email and a direct line. Treat "Kingsley is the portal lead" as UNVERIFIED in the strict sense; "Kingsley is the lead recruiter" is well supported.

ZERO INCOMING GUARD TRANSFERS. I checked every Yale roster from 2022-23 through 2026-27 for prior-college annotations. Across five rosters, exactly one player carries one: Connor May "(WashU)". Every other player on all five rosters lists a high school or prep school. So portal_guards_in is genuinely empty — not "I couldn't find any," but "the rosters affirmatively show none."

DIRECTION OF FLOW. Yale is a portal EXPORTER, not an importer. Recent outbound: Danny Wolf → Michigan, Matt Knowling → USC, Samson Aletan → Providence, Isaac Celiscar into the portal. WTNH coverage framed the closing portal window as a period of uncertainty for Jones's program because of losses. They restock through high school and prep, not the portal.

PIPELINE PROFILE. The 2026-27 roster is heavily prep/independent-school: Choate Rosemary Hall, Albany Academy, The Bishop's School, Saint Ignatius College Prep, The Neighborhood Academy, Salesian College Prep. This is an academically-gated pipeline, which is consistent with the admissions constraint above.

WHY THE MAY PRECEDENT IS THE USEFUL DATA POINT HERE. It is the single most relevant fact I found: within the last four months, this exact staff took a D3 undergraduate, and Jones spoke publicly and positively about the move. The route is real and freshly walked. It also shows what the route required — a decorated D3 producer moving with eligibility remaining and clearing admissions.

YES — and notably, the only college-to-college addition they have made in this entire span came from D3.

Connor May, F, 6-6, Palatine, Ill. — transferred from Washington University in St. Louis (D3, UAA) to Yale, announced 22 April 2026, arriving as a junior on the 2026-27 roster (#21). Yale's own 28 July 2026 release "Men's Basketball Welcomes Six to 2026-27 Roster" explicitly identifies him as a junior transfer from WashU and quotes Jones on him bringing "experience, size and a history of success."

His D3 résumé at the time of the move: UAA Rookie of the Year (2024-25), then 17.3 ppg / 7.2 rpg as a sophomore with NABC Third Team All-America honors; WashU made the D3 Final Four (2025) and Sweet 16 (2026).

Two caveats that matter: (a) he is a forward, not a guard; (b) n=1. No D2, NAIA, or JUCO additions found on any roster 2022-23 through 2026-27.

Mechanism worth noting: his announcement was reported as "pending admissions." He moved as an UNDERGRAD with eligibility left, which is the only workable path — the Ivy League does not let graduate students compete, so the transfer must clear Yale's regular (very selective) undergraduate transfer admissions office, not just the coaching staff. A coach's interest is necessary but not sufficient here.
